met_analysis:
The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” [Pronunciation: Akvan] over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards with the speed of 12 kmph during past 06 hours and lies centered at 0530 hours IST of today, the 19th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 14.5°N and Longitude 85.3°E, about 440 km east- southeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 440 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 580 km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 530 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 590 km south of Puri (Odisha). It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sikkim & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian sea & adjoining south Lakshadweep area extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Bangladesh & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The feeble Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 33°N persists.
